A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMLRANK research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, moves, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results on debiasing, auxiliary judges, acquisition policies, and BT misspecification, plus analyses of Chatbot Arena and MT-Bench preference data.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical analyses, updates acquisition results, and adds a Chatbot Arena experiment using alternative prompt embeddings.

M1.justification: Appendix C changes optional scoring functions: softmax/Plackett–Luce, soft-Copeland, Kemeny, and judge-miscalibration examples are replaced by thresholded-dominance and worst-case/soft-minimum scores. The core cross-fitted EIF estimator, judge-as-features procedure, and acquisition algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nonlinear-tie and BT-misspecification simulations, Chatbot Arena, and MT-Bench. The added embedding experiment reuses Chatbot Arena data and the same preference-ranking task; it changes representation rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain plug-in estimators, the BT-restricted debiased estimator in Figure 4b, and random acquisition in Table 2. The new embedding experiment uses the existing plug-in/debiased comparison, without introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix N.2 adds an experimental configuration using 100-dimensional text-embedding-3-small representations instead of 100-dimensional TF-IDF plus SVD features. The original experiment remains, with its previously specified splits, nuisance-model settings, budgets, and metrics retained.

E4.justification: Appendix N.2 and Figure 6 add a sensitivity check of rankings and confidence intervals to prompt representation. Existing judge-quality and BT-misspecification analyses remain. MT-Bench results are retained from v1 Appendix L as v2 Appendix N.1, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Table 2 increases the reported acquisition-experiment repetition count from 15 to 50 runs. The mean-and-95%-CI reporting convention and the existing Gaussian-max and Bonferroni procedures for simultaneous intervals are retained.

E6.justification: Table 2 updates A-optimal/random MSE means, in its reported scale: Borda 0.108/0.133 to 0.130/0.141, BT 2.565/2.910 to 2.861/2.974, and rank centrality 0.010/0.017 to 0.017/0.020, with revised CIs. These summaries accompany the changed run count and retain the same mean ordering. Figure 6 adds ranking results under alternative embeddings, rather than demonstrating a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: New Theorem B.2 and its proof bound the excess MSE of plug-in acquisition relative to oracle acquisition using nuisance-estimation error, under additional conditions. Appendix C replaces several formal target definitions, while Appendix D expands the BT-recovery argument already sketched in v1 Appendix E.2. These extend the existing theory without replacing its central inference or optimality results.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: generalized ranking scores, efficient debiased inference with auxiliary judges, and cost-optimal preference acquisition. The new conclusion summarizes these claims; the experimental-purpose clarification does not redefine them.

C2.justification: New Section 8 discusses instability from small propensities, possible stabilization, limits concerning complex agent systems, and partial identification as future work. Basic missing-at-random and positivity caveats already appeared in v1 Appendix B.1. New Appendix J develops the causal-inference analogy, and Appendix N.2 interprets the embedding results as robust.

D1.justification: The code-access pointer changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository to a named GitHub repository. Appendix N.2 identifies text-embedding-3-small and its 100-dimensional configuration. Existing LightGBM tuning grids and implementation details are retained; repository availability was not externally checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Mukherjee et al. (2024) and van der Laan and Van Der Laan (2026), and Appendix D explicitly distinguishes the contextual log-odds projection from HodgeRank-style formulations. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 adds a discussion/conclusion and explanatory appendix material, moves the existing external-judge paragraph into Section 5.4, adds a conflict disclosure, and copyedits the prose. The main narrative and most existing wording remain, so the reorganization is limited.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are revised, Figure 3 is enlarged and recaptioned, Table 1 gains coverage highlighting, and Figure 6 is added. Existing display structures largely remain. Figure 3's revised caption names a common baseline, although its retained annotations still follow the different panel-specific references described in v1.

improvement.justification: The acquisition-error bound, 50-run acquisition summaries, embedding sensitivity check, and clearer practical limitations modestly strengthen support and transparency beyond v1. The core method and most validation were already present. These gains outweigh localized weaknesses, including Figure 3's caption/annotation mismatch and insufficient qualification of the new nonsmooth score examples against the retained differentiability assumptions.
